text:
jess: quick check — posted a compact preview mock for suppressions + channel list. trying to land a single-row preview for alerting panels, but there's weird vertical jitter when toggling dense mode. screenshot: https://redwood.design/s/compact-preview.png

mike: saw it — the jitter looks like line-height collapsing when the preview expands. repro: toggle dense -> expand preview -> collapse.

leila: agree. also noticed the keyboard focus jumps to the last interactive element in the preview instead of the preview header. a11y snag.

toni: copy nit: we use both "snooze" and "mute" across flows. can we pick one? customers get confused which pauses notifications vs suppresses incidents.

jess: good call. proposal: use "snooze" for time-based pauses, "mute" reserved for channel-level silences. thoughts?

sam: +1 for that taxonomy. but update helptext: "Snooze — pause alerts for X duration; Mute — silence this channel for all alerts." small copy tweak.

mike: for the jitter, short-term fix: set explicit line-height on the preview container. long-term: audit CSS transitions on the nested badges. patch suggestion:

```
.preview-row { line-height: 20px; transition: none; }
.preview-expanded { transition: height 120ms ease-out; }
```

leila: for keyboard, add roving tabindex and ensure header gets focus on expand. also add `aria-expanded` and an `aria-live="polite"` region that announces "Preview expanded".

ux-bot: accessibility check flagged: color contrast for the "snooze" pill in dark theme is 3.4:1 — needs 4.5:1 for small UI text.

toni: great catch. we can darken the pill bg by 8% and bump text to 600 weight. small but improves scannability.

jess: design question — when channels list is long, the preview pushes the channel chooser off-screen. should preview overlay or push? pros/cons: overlay keeps chooser stable but hides context; push maintains spatial relation but confuses keyboard users.

sam: prefer overlay that pins to the right edge and traps focus, with Esc to close. avoids layout shift for dense views. but ensure screen readers are told preview is a dialog: role=dialog + aria-modal=true.

mike: overlay needs a subtle entrance to avoid perceived flicker. 160ms fade + 80ms slide from right feels smooth. avoid scaling transforms (can break GPU).

leila: accessibility addition: when preview opens, announce channel context: "Preview for channel X — press Esc to close." use `aria-describedby` to read the helptext.

toni: copy suggestion for the preview header: instead of "Notification preview" try "How this alert will notify <channel>" — more explicit and scannable.

jess: I like explicit. maybe shorter: "How this alert notifies <channel>" — fits space better.

sam: about suppression scheduling UX — current date picker is modal heavy. can we inline quick presets (1h, 4h, 24h) + custom dropdown? frequent pattern is quick fixes.

mike: add a small local history shorthand: "Last snoozes" showing recent durations defaulting to org policy. quick tap to reapply.

leila: for screen reader users, presets should be buttons with clear aria-labels: e.g. `aria-label=\"Snooze for 1 hour\"`. prefer not to rely only on visual tokens.

jess: action items: 1) mike to ship CSS line-height patch + fade timing (ETA: today). 2) leila to prototype roving tabindex + live-region announce (ETA: tomorrow). 3) toni to consolidate snooze/mute copy across product (ETA: Friday). 4) sam to prototype overlay dialog pattern and keyboard trap (ETA: Thu). I'll reconcile and post updated mock.

toni: small follow-up — telemetry: add an event when preview opens with `preview_mode: compact|expanded` and `channel_count`. helps measure if compact is used.

mike: i'll add the telemetry ping in the preview open handler. sample event: `analytics.track('preview.open', { mode: 'compact', channel_count: 12 })`.

leila: accessibility QA note: once fixes land, let's run axe+NVDA pass, plus a quick keyboard-only smoke test.

jess: thanks everyone — will post updated files in Figma and ping here when ready :thumbsup:
